gates.title: Package, CLI and discovery -- port the prototype behind a real entrypoint
gates.task: Stand up scripts/code_map/ as the repo's FIRST Python package under scripts/ and move the prototype (astx.py, supplement.py, render_map.py) behind a real CLI with argparse. This is a PORT in the checkable sense: NO defect fixes and NO schema changes (those are g2/g3/g4). Do NOT claim 'no behavior change' -- it is unfalsifiable here, because the prototype hardcodes ROOT to an external repo and has no argparse, so there is no prior behavior to diff against (critic F7). The prototype is SIX modules, not three: astx.py, supplement.py, render_map.py, render.py, render_fn.py, and the checks pair. render_fn.py imports `render as R`; render.py was recovered from evidence/x11 and is now present, so the import graph closes. The prototype hardcodes ROOT to an external repo and has no argparse at all, so nothing downstream can run until this exists. Add a discovery layer that enumerates the corpus from git ls-files and EXCLUDES .agent-work/. Add the narrow .gitignore entries for the statement store, supplement and position cache -- .agent-work/ is deliberately TRACKED in this repo so a blanket scratch rule is wrong. Verify the installer's runtime-closure tests still pass: _direct_runtime_siblings resolves siblings as scripts/<name>.py and is blind to a package directory, so confirm this package does not silently fall outside the bundling machinery.
gates.close: python scripts/code_map/cli.py --root <repo> enumerates exactly the 103-file corpus and runs extract->supplement->render end to end; full existing suite still green

gates.title: A check stage that can fail
gates.depends: g0 -- there must be a pipeline to check
gates.task: REWRITE the prototype's checks; do not port them. They are print-only today: no assertions, no exit code, so they read as measurements and never as a passing suite. Deliver assertions with nonzero exit and thresholds committed against THIS corpus (103 files / 3,411 entities / 52,292 lines), never the prototype's 1,224-file numbers -- otherwise the first CI run is the experiment. Cover: determinism (rebuild twice, byte-identical, no non-empty diff on unchanged source); referenced-by semantics (count AND module list against an independent source scan); edge recall per predicate with a floor, including `writes` where the independent oracle is blind; hole count against a committed baseline; template-ASCII by exact-line provenance; and the CHURN RATIO with its 3x ceiling (critic TS6's disposition attaches a re-measurement gate to the build queue, because g4/g5/g6 move that number in opposite directions -- this gate owns the threshold, g9 owns the re-run).
gates.close: each of these six falsifiers has a test that FAILS when its property is broken, proven by deliberate mutation, with a nonzero exit: (1) determinism -- any non-empty diff on unchanged source; (2) inbound-edge attribution -- any page whose caller set differs from an independent full scan; (3) extraction correctness -- a symbol an independent scan resolves that the AST pass misses, outside the named inference-rule gaps, plus a hand-labelled edge sample per predicate below its recall floor; (4) churn boundedness -- ratio above 3x; (5) redundancy rule -- a page whose non-recoverable lines are a minority; (6) authored-layer staleness -- a tag whose anchor body changed while its text did not, going unflagged
gates.command: python -m pytest tests/ -q  AND  python -m pytest tests/test_code_map.py -k 'code_map_checks' -q
constraints: thresholds are measured against this repo's corpus and committed, not inherited
a check that cannot go red is not a check -- prove each one fails under mutation

the FULL suite must be green at this gate boundary, not just this gate's own tests (critic F6) -- the targeted selector proves this gate added a test that can fail, the full run proves it broke nothing else

NO absolute-count thresholds (critic F4): this run itself adds .py files to the corpus it measures, so 3,411 entities / 52,292 lines / any hole integer is stale before g2 finishes. Express every threshold as a ratio or as an invariant recomputed from the corpus at run time -- 'zero collisions remain', not 'all 4 resolve'; 'holes <= X% of entities', not a committed integer

constraint: checks must be able to fail
decision: committed thresholds -- sized to this corpus; durable, every later gate is measured against them
confidence_flags: prototype measurements come from a different repo and do NOT transfer

gates.title: D2 -- function-nested definitions drop the method from their symbol
gates.depends: g1 -- the regression must be able to go red before it is fixed
gates.task: astx.py:_func emits mod:{clsstack[-1]}.{name} whenever ANY class is on the stack, regardless of how deep inside a method the definition sits. So a closure defined inside Class.test_x is emitted as mod:Class.<closure> -- the METHOD name is dropped, not the class. Two same-named closures in two methods of one class therefore collide, merge their caller sets, and both pages show the union. A class defined inside a function is separately named as if module-level. MEASURED ON THIS REPO: exactly 4 real collisions, all of the closure-folded-onto-its-class shape, listed in .agent-work/issue-456/reference/d2_collisions.txt (probe: reference/probe_d2.py, which simulates the extractor's actual rule rather than a model of it). Write the failing test against those 4 named collisions FIRST -- no external repo and no fixture needed. Then put the enclosing METHOD into the symbol for function-nested definitions.
gates.close: each of the 4 named collisions in d2_collisions.txt resolves to a distinct symbol that CARRIES THE METHOD NAME, and the reproducer goes red-then-green. NOT sufficient: any fix that merely makes collisions distinct without naming the method -- a class qualifier satisfies 'collisions resolve' without touching the defect (critic F2)
gates.command: python -m pytest tests/ -q  AND  python -m pytest tests/test_code_map.py -k 'code_map_symbol_identity' -q
constraints: red before green -- the reproducer must be committed failing first

the FULL suite must be green at this gate boundary, not just this gate's own tests (critic F6) -- the targeted selector proves this gate added a test that can fail, the full run proves it broke nothing else
